observation: Architecture critique CRITICAL-1 caught a wrong-rationale defect that would have shipped a no-op abort: plan justified builtin tool-revocation as 'loop breaks, no further registry.invoke', but builtin skips registry.invoke entirely (provisioning L645) and runs tools internally in runLoop. The real revocation is stopSession->aborted->runLoop. A builder following the literal rationale ships an abort that does nothing for the only adapter AC5 exercises. Cold-spot critique reading the actual adapter code (not the plan's claim) prevented it.

Non-AC plan deliverables shipped UNTESTED against their own plan-stated test contracts. Spec §'what's genuinely missing' items (lifecycle-propagation retry, Z8-050 adapter gating) are not numbered ACs, so the red phase wrote AC tests but skipped the §7/§8 assertions the plan explicitly promised. Code was correct; the pre-existing §7 coverage was tautological (asserted appliedLogs.length >= 1, passes under both old double-log and new in-place behavior). Caught at Phase-4 review as M1/M2, fixed in one cycle. Red phase should treat plan-promised test assertions for NON-AC deliverables as first-class, not optional.

Architecture critique WARNING-2 caught an admission-error-on-detached-path hole created by the 200->202 admit/run split: a MissingCredential-class failure that only manifests at P9 harness.startSession (local mode, builtin, no resolvedModel) would land in the detached .catch->crashSession AFTER the 202 returned, breaking the plan's claim that the 500 mapping is preserved. Fix: synchronous resolvedModel presence guard in admitSession pre-P5-insert. Honest contract kept, no doomed row inserted. Splitting a synchronous request into admit+detached-run requires re-validating that every error class still throws before the detach boundary.

Builder's enforceResolvedModelGuard flag (default false; true only on the HTTP startSessionProvision path) correctly reconciled two conflicting contracts: WARNING-2's HTTP-500-on-missing-credential vs AD2's dispatcher path where a missing credential is unrecoverable-per-task (dropped from queue) and fixtures run builtin stubs needing no resolved model. A plan-vs-reality resolution that scopes a guard by call-site rather than weakening either contract. Code review verified it weakens no AC. Pattern: when two entry points share a phase implementation but have different error-handling contracts, gate the strict check by a per-call-site flag, not globally.

Contract-change ripple: changing POST /api/sessions 200->202 (work accepted, not done) rippled into a mandatory protected-tests enumeration (R1 'returns 200' assertions rewritten to 'assert 202 + active, then poll until done/crashed') AND a SessionConfig.sessionId type-ripple across every adapter test's inline config. Anticipated in the plan §13 protected-tests list (closed the lone Dimension-9/CC-008 miss) so it was deliberate, not a surprise at test:all. Status-code changes on an existing route are a recurring ripple cost; enumerating callers at plan-time (CC-008/CC-021) contained it.

Concept probe correctly held the 'wiring-only, no new primitive' line (concept-present, 1 round). Essence probes (Session-is-not-Task, Dispatch-is-not-Execution, Handoff-is-not-session_ended) became load-bearing constraints the architecture honored: the Handoff-never-emits-session_ended rule drove the rowcount-gated CAS emit invariant (§4.3), and Dispatch-is-not-Execution drove the admit/run 202 split (§2). Fast concept confirmation that still produced the invariants downstream phases depended on.

AF6->AF7 handoff steer was precise and paid off: AF6 retro flagged (i) dispatcher one-line wiring with adapterPool/workspaceAdapter/workspaceBasePath in scope, (ii) generic-routine auto-fire once wired, (iii) two DEFERRED-AC fragments (per-run-cap, daily-digest) carried to AF7. AF7's §1 boot-wiring matched the steer exactly (setProvisionSessionFn + dispatcherDeps). Cross-workpackage handoff notes in the retro log measurably reduced AF7 discovery cost.
